title: Warhost for Godot 4 is live: 48 army battles, every soldier and banner drawn in code
html:
Warhost is live for Godot 4: army battles for your 2D game. Give it two armies as plain data and the battle plays out soldier by soldier on a field it paints, then hands the survivors of every regiment back to your game. 48 staged battles ship as presets on 12 fields.

What it does

  • Regiments of foot, pikes, archers, horse and mages, each with a name and a soldier count. Four formations (line, wedge, square, loose), each with written rules.
  • Every soldier is drawn in its army's colours; volleys arc overhead, spells burst, riders charge, regiments break and run.
  • Every regiment flies a banner whose arms are generated from its name. A banner leans back when its regiment breaks and falls where its last man falls.
  • When it ends, a signal hands back the war record: the winner, and for every regiment how many stood, fled and fell. A host of any size is carried at several soldiers per figure, and the numbers still add up to the man.

Tested

  • Every battle photographed under Forward+ and Compatibility: 96 frames, zero engine errors, all 48 distinct under each renderer.
  • The shipped zip installed into a blank Godot 4.7.2 project under both renderers: the Readme example run as written, every regiment accounted for, the same seed fighting the same battle, a host of 99,999 soldiers, banners for 500 names, and three presets dropped in and photographed.
  • 6 attacks, including a path with spaces and non Latin characters, a third renderer, a renamed addon folder, and one battle of 480 figures timed with vsync off while eight battles at once were run and reported; 213 Readme claims checked against the shipped files.
  • Looking at the pictures found what no counter could. The first full gate passed battles that were recolours of each other, flying the very same banners; two hosts folded into one ball because men and horses kept the same distance; an aftermath read as a fight still going on; a gold sword vanished on a gold saltire. The gate passed every one of them. All were fixed before release.

Free lite

The page carries a free MIT lite: 12 of the 48 battles, fought with foot and archers alone, the code cut to those two arms, with its own demo.

Where this line stands: 25 Godot listings live from this studio, 3 purchases so far (read from the store the day this went live).

Disclosure: the scripts, presets and demo were written with AI, and everything they draw is computed by that code; the cover is the pack's own render with the title set on it.
